newsitem.title: USA: Labor board issues complaint against WHX.
newsitem.headline: Labor board issues complaint against WHX.

text.p: The National Labor Relations Board issued an unfair labor practice complaint against WHX Corp's Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel unit for allegedly firing two non-union office workers who refused to cross a union picket line, the United Steelworkers union said Monday.

In a news release, the USW said the board alleged that the company fired two sales correspondents for refusing to perform work in its steel operations, where union workers have been on strike since October 1.
The NLRB alleged that the company fired the employees to discourage membership in the union. As a result, it said, the terminations were unlawful.
A hearing on the complaint is scheduled for May 29. If it is upheld, the fired employees would be eligible for back pay and reinstatement to their former jobs.
About 4,500 steelworkers have been on strike against Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel since October 1. The strike has idled eight steel plants in three states.
